signals.source_text: Why did Network School choose Kazakhstan over 10+ countries? A new conversation with Balaji Srinivasan has just premiered across Trusted Kazakhstan, Astana Hub, and Network State Podcast. Network School is building a global community for people who want to learn tech, work remotely, build companies, and live alongside other ambitious people. Kazakhstan is set to become one of the first major global hubs for this model. In the conversation, Balaji Srinivasan, founder of Network School and former CTO of Coinbase, joins Rinata Ilyubayeva , Managing Director at Astana Hub, and host Thorsten Gutmann to discuss why Kazakhstan stood out among more than 10 countries considered for Network School’s expansion. The discussion goes beyond the decision itself. It explores: • why Astana can become a destination for global tech talent • how digital nomads can contribute to Kazakhstan’s innovation ecosystem • new approaches to education and lifelong learning • how global and local talent can build companies together • Kazakhstan’s growing focus on AI, emerging technologies, and new industries • what the cities and communities of the future could look like One of the central ideas of the conversation is simple: Kazakhstan has the opportunity not only to attract global talent, but to create an environment where people can build, scale, and take tech to international markets. For us at Astana Hub, this is also part of a broader ambition: to make Kazakhstan a place where international founders, engineers, creators, and investors can connect with local talent and build globally competitive tech businesses. Watch the full conversation: https://lnkd.in/eCDdXhGU Join Network School: https://ns.com/ Join the opening of Network School in Astana on September 2: https://luma.com/nskz Meet the global tech community at AI & Digital Bridge, October 1-3 in Astana: https://lnkd.in/d8j2HPmf

signals.source_text: The same conversation has come up more than once this year, and it always starts the same way, in my messages here. Someone in their early thirties who has taken over a family business. One version of them wants no part of what they inherited and is building something separate. Another is trying to take it to the moon. And a third doesnt know which way to turn. Different directions. Same question underneath. Which part of this is mine. They are usually moving quickly and have ambitious plans. What they have not checked is whose definition of winning they are running on. Most are a little annoyed when I ask. The idea is not to slow down. It is to make sure the direction is theirs before they spend another five years going that way at speed. If you recognised yourself somewhere in the last few weeks of posts, that is usually the signal. My messages are open.
